28.translation: 23 representative layers were rendered in the three main modes using 69 explicitly synthetic geometry fixtures: 59 succeeded and 10 were rejected by contract, including automatic primer labels. Centre labels support bp/aa in single-sequence chord/circular views; primers and restriction layers require DNA. Help now clarifies these boundaries. This verifies mode boundaries, not all parameter combinations, biological recognition or devices. See the [complete runtime record](⟦shared:0⟧).

30.translation: ⟦shared:1⟧ in ⟦shared:0⟧ explicitly checks circular parameters and conflicts involving automatic orientation or segments. Runtime validation also checks general data contracts and nucleotide-only restrictions. Current source files accompany the site under ⟦shared:2⟧; reference pages are generated from current roxygen/Rd.

31.translation: A Position controls local placement; it cannot convert an unsupported layer into a different coordinate layer. Outside/inside means above/below in collinear mode and follows the outward/inward local normal in circular mode. Re-read the result when transferring settings. See [four direction concepts](⟦shared:0⟧) for display direction versus biological strand.

33.translation: See [installation](⟦shared:0⟧) for setup instructions and [migration](⟦shared:1⟧) when updating existing scripts. Single circular mode requires one displayed sequence. Circular protein layout is a display choice, not a claim of molecular circularity. Project mixed bp/aa inputs first or plot them separately.

35.translation: The [Dotplot/Radial support matrix](⟦shared:0⟧) records the new contracts. Dotplot uses a dedicated identity HSP mark. Radial adapts the existing feature/Track frames with cyclic adjacency; circular-only layers, shared straight scales and branches are explicitly rejected. The current layer probes are recorded separately from the earlier three-view evidence.

40.translation:
[Fusion](⟦shared:0⟧) accepts registered Circular/Chord/Collinear/Sankey/Radial plots, nested Fusions and explicitly registered Cartesian character details. Eight named sides and explicit angle/box placements share the source-frame resolver. Each panel keeps its existing layer contract. Cross-panel interval
fronts use one-based inclusive boundaries with continuous curve mapping;
fully visible same-unit source intervals and unambiguous panel/instance routes
are required. Generic Fusion scales affect cross-panel layers only. Dotplot, facets and implicit third-party coordinate adapters remain unregistered. Physical panels are remeasured at save time; this does not imply
global collision avoidance or general font scaling.

45.translation: The [aligned-character workflow](⟦shared:0⟧) uses ordinary ggplot x/y coordinates. Source positions and alignment columns are separate fields. Final physical glyph measurement selects readable text or explicit tile/error behavior; it does not change source data or shrink fonts. Explicit source registration supports Fusion/magnify details. Optional source-backed CDS translation uses Biostrings and the existing CDS map; no alignment or missing phase is inferred. See [CDS translation](⟦shared:1⟧) and [character details](⟦shared:2⟧).

47.translation:
[⟦shared:0⟧](⟦shared:1⟧) supports individual Chord, Circular,
Collinear, Sankey, Radial and Dotplot plots, and opted-in Fusion panels.
It scales default theme styles and arranges native guides under explicit user
constraints; no policy is applied by default. Facets, arbitrary custom grobs,
outer Fusion allocations and a global label solver are outside this scope.

48.translation: [Magnification](⟦shared:0⟧) supports independent registered details with explicit per-row targets, eight named sides, nested leaf paths and free boxes. Deliberate overlap is opt-in; global avoidance is separate.

49.translation: Fusion also supports Sankey/Radial, layered compositions and eight named sides or explicit boxes. Leaf-panel paths preserve independent sources, and deliberate overlaps export their paint order. Dotplot still requires independent axis registration. See [Advanced boxes and nesting](⟦shared:0⟧).
